  • Method Details

    • style

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> style(ControlStyle style)
      Phase 18s follow-up — selects the trigger's visual style. ControlStyle.MK (default) uses MenuKit's RAISED-panel look; ControlStyle.VANILLA uses Minecraft's standard widget/button sprite atlas (square corners, gray gradient). The popover always stays RAISED regardless — popover is a container for choices, not itself a button.

    • at

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> at(int childX, int childY)
      Panel-local position. Default (0, 0).

    • triggerSize

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> triggerSize(int width, int height)
      Required: trigger width × height in pixels. Vanilla button-style default is 120×20. Popover width matches trigger width.

    • items

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> items(List<T> items)
      Required: the items to display in the popover. Defensively copied at build time — mutating the supplied list post-build does not affect the dropdown. Empty list throws at build().

    • label

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> label(Function<T, net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> labelFn)
      Required: function to produce the displayed text for an item. Used both for the trigger (with current selection) and for each popover row.

    • selection

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> selection(Supplier<@Nullable T> supplier, Consumer<T> consumer)
      Required: lens pair for the current selection. Library reads supplier each frame to render the trigger label; library calls consumer when the user picks an item from the popover.

      Selection identity uses T.equals(). null supplier values OK (renders empty trigger). Consumer is invoked only when the picked item differs from the current selection.

    • maxVisibleItems

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> maxVisibleItems(int n)
      Optional: cap the number of popover rows visible at once. When items.size() > maxVisibleItems, an internal scrollbar appears on the popover's right edge. Default 8.

    • itemTooltip

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> itemTooltip(Function<T, net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> fn)
      Optional: per-item tooltip function. When set, hovering a popover row queues fn.apply(item) as the next-frame tooltip — companion to the trigger-level AbstractPanelElement.tooltip(Component) helper. Trigger and item tooltips are mutually exclusive in time (trigger fires only when popover is closed; item fires only when open), so they coexist without competing.

      Returning null from fn for a given item suppresses the tooltip for that row.

    • disabledWhen

      public Dropdown.Builder<T> disabledWhen(BooleanSupplier disabledWhen)
      Optional disabled predicate (Phase 3b — Item 8). When it returns true, the trigger renders disabled (VANILLA → widget/button_disabled sprite; MK → PanelStyle.DARK panel) and all interaction is ignored — clicks/scroll/keys no-op and any open popover force-closes. Per-frame predicate shape, matching Button/Toggle's disabledWhen. Default: always enabled.

    • spec

      public ElementSpec spec()
      Layout terminal (Phase 3b — Item 6). Returns an ElementSpec for use in Row / Column.

      Reported dimensions are the TRIGGER footprint (.triggerSize(w, h)), not the popover. By design the popover overflows the trigger's layout bounds — it renders via Dropdown.renderOverlay(RenderContext) on the overlay pass and claims its own input region via Dropdown.getActiveOverlayBounds(), exactly like its hit-test/overlay model. So Row/Column reserves only the trigger footprint; the open popover paints on top of whatever follows it in the layout, which is the intended behavior (popovers are transient and z-ordered above siblings).

      The layout helper calls ElementSpec.at(int, int), which re-runs this builder's configuration positioned at the computed coordinates.
